source_binding.method: Fetched immutable raw.githubusercontent.com files for target commit; SHA-256 and Git blob OIDs recomputed from exact bytes.

receiver_guard.semantics: IsLocalCalling distinguishes local Binder transport from remote Databus; it does not authorize a caller identity. IsSamgrCall reads the receiving process ProcessSkeleton::GetSamgrFlag(), not the incoming caller UID/PID. Therefore the handler is restricted to a stub in a SAMGR-marked receiver process, but this predicate is not an ACL on the requestor.
receiver_guard.effect: The generic stub special-code switch dispatches GET_GRANTED_SESSION_NAME to this handler.

identity_provenance.code: GetGrantedSessionName reads IPCSkeleton::GetCallingPid() and GetCallingUid(), then calls CreateSessionName(uid,pid).
identity_provenance.semantics: These values are the kernel/Binder caller identity for the current transaction, obtained through the active IPC invoker. When the intended nested path is a service stub calling its SAMGR proxy, SAMGR sees that service process UID/PID, not the original app that earlier called the service. If a direct local app-to-SAMGR transaction existed, SAMGR would see that app's UID/PID.
identity_provenance.name: DBINDER_SOCKET_NAME_PREFIX + decimal uid + '_' + decimal pid
identity_provenance.grant_target: In the intended GetSessionName nested call, the granted SoftBus name maps to the requesting service's own process identity. No parcel-supplied UID/PID are accepted on this path.

samgr_proxy_and_export.proxy: IPCObjectStub::GetSessionName obtains IPCProcessSkeleton::GetCurrent()->GetSAMgrObject(), requires a proxy object, and calls IPCObjectProxy::GetGrantedSessionName().
samgr_proxy_and_export.typed_get_granted_helper: Declared in ipc_object_proxy.h but absent from pinned libipc_single_map; the ipc_core GN target is a prebuilt symlink to libipc_single.z.so, which is built with this version map. No standard exported typed helper for direct ordinary-app invocation was established.
samgr_proxy_and_export.generic_route: IPCObjectProxy::GetGrantedSessionName uses SendRequestInner with the special transaction directly. Public generic SendRequest enforces the special-code limit; prior pinned D8/T13/T15 evidence found no ordinary generic route for special session-management codes.
samgr_proxy_and_export.indirect_app_route: The distinct IPCObjectProxy::GetSessionName helper is declared and exported in libipc_single_map. A caller holding a proxy to a service stub can issue GET_SESSION_NAME; that service stub then makes the nested SAMGR call described above. This causes the target service to request/grant its own DBinder session name. It is a supported DBinder lifecycle operation and does not grant the caller's UID/PID under this chain.
samgr_proxy_and_export.ordinary_app_qualification: A proxy holder can reach the exported GetSessionName code path in the pinned native inner-kit ABI. Whether a third-party app can link this platformsdk inner-kit in the shipped product is not proven by source metadata. Direct access to the internal GetGrantedSessionName helper is not exported in the standard map.

grant_and_cleanup_accounting.ipc_grant: Each successful GET_SESSION_NAME request that reaches the service's GetSessionName causes one nested GET_GRANTED_SESSION_NAME; the SAMGR-side handler calls CreateSessionName once, which calls DBinderSoftbusClient::DBinderGrantPermission once.
grant_and_cleanup_accounting.ipc_refcount: In the IPC SoftBus client, each grant for an existing socketName increments mapSessionRefCount_[socketName] once and calls the dynamically loaded SoftBus grant function; a first grant inserts count 1 and calls it. This is per unique sessionName key, so repeated requests do not allocate a new IPC map key per call.
grant_and_cleanup_accounting.remove: DBinderRemovePermission decrements the same name's IPC refcount once per RemoveSessionName transaction; it invokes the backend SoftBus remove only when the count reaches zero (or below).
teardown_call_sites: DatabusSocketListener::ServerOnShutdown calls RemoveSessionName once per callback after obtaining the invoker.
DatabusSocketListener::ClientOnShutdown calls RemoveSessionName once per callback after obtaining the invoker.

Both funnel through IPCProcessSkeleton::RemoveSoftbusServer, which snapshots sessionName_ and sends exactly one IPCObjectProxy::RemoveSessionName(sessionName) call. Repository search found no other production call site of RemoveSoftbusServer in the reviewed IPC source scope.
grant_and_cleanup_accounting.matching: A GET_SESSION_NAME request alone is not paired with a RemoveSessionName call. The usual successful DBinder setup obtains the name before InvokeListenThread and later a socket shutdown callback removes once for the relevant process session; one shutdown does not mechanically replay or count all earlier GET requests. Repeated name queries that do not proceed to a corresponding databus lifecycle can therefore leave extra IPC refcounts. Exact one-GET-to-one-socket correspondence across retries, listener reuse, and failed setup was not established from this route review.
grant_and_cleanup_accounting.softbus_backend: IPC's pinned DBinderSoftbusClient source passes uid, pid and socketName to dynamically resolved DBinderGrantPermission, and passes socketName to DBinderRemovePermission. The available separate local DSoftBus source delegates these to ClientGrantPermission -> ServerIpcGrantPermission and ClientRemovePermission -> ServerIpcRemovePermission. No target product manifest/build lock pairs a DSoftBus revision with IPC bbb92..., so backend permission storage/deduplication/authorization semantics are not claimed as target-product facts.

candidate_decision.claim: A caller that can reach the exported GetSessionName helper may cause a target service to request a grant for that service's own uid_pid name. Repeated requests not followed by a databus lifecycle can increment SAMGR's same-name IPC refcount without a matching shutdown decrement, potentially keeping the service's own dynamic name permission reference alive longer than intended.
candidate_decision.why_not_a_vulnerability_finding: The route's identity is the target service, not the app; only one same-name IPC map entry is shown; DSoftBus backend semantics are not target-paired; no evidence shows the residual grant lets an untrusted caller impersonate the service, access another UID/PID, bypass an authorization check, exhaust a bounded permission table, or cause material impact. This is a lifecycle/refcount question for T40/L2, not a confirmed cross-subject authorization flaw.
candidate_decision.ordinary_app_path: Indirect exported GetSessionName route exists for a proxy holder, but third-party package/API policy and typical system-service proxy availability in the target product remain unbound. Direct GetGrantedSessionName helper is absent from the standard version map.
candidate_decision.verdict: insufficient_for_security_finding; retain only one conditional observation for independent T40 challenge; do not send as confirmed vulnerability

t40_rebuttal_points: Can an ordinary third-party app in the target product link the exported inner-kit GetSessionName helper and obtain a proxy to a stub whose DBinderGetSessionName accepts the transaction?
Does every successful GetSessionName trigger a distinct server listener/socket and exactly one shutdown removal, or can repeated queries/retries/failures accumulate IPC refcounts without sockets?

Does a retained same-name refcount have any authorization effect beyond keeping the service's own name registration/permission alive; can another identity exploit it or is it only self-identity availability?

Confirm target-paired DSoftBus permission implementation: whether grants are deduplicated by name, whether repeated same-name grants consume bounded slots, and what exact authorization the UID/PID/name tuple enforces.
Consider stress feasibility only after defining a concrete external effect; don't infer integer-overflow/DoS from the signed counter without a realistic call rate and observable impact.
limitations: IPC code is immutably bound to target commit bbb92dbb2f52aca54ab268307c9476ac1802f3ff, but no product lock/build record proves the deployed SDK or DSoftBus pairing.
